title: The King and His Vizier's Garden
summary: To persuade the king to practice restraint, the First Vizier recounted the story of King Shahriman of Persia:
keywords: the king and his wazir's wife
full_text:
To persuade the king to practice restraint, the First Vizier recounted the story of King Shahriman of Persia:

'King Shahriman, while walking through the private quarters of his capital, caught a glimpse of the wife of his Grand Vizier. She was a lady of celebrated intellect, dignity, and virtue. Tempted by selfish impulse, the king visited the vizier's mansion while his minister was inspecting the frontier fortresses.

The noble lady received her monarch with serene composure, conducted him to the garden pavilion, and served him cool sherbet.

When the king looked upon her with inappropriate admiration, she smiled with modest gravity and said: "Sire, if a mighty lion enters a humble farmer’s orchard, will he crush the delicate jasmine flowers, or will he protect the garden from the wild beasts?"

The king was struck by the delicate nobility of her reprimand. Realizing that to dishonor his most faithful minister's home was an act of base treachery unworthy of a monarch, Shahriman felt profound shame.

He rose from the divan, left his royal signet ring upon the marble table as a token of reverence, and departed into the night without having uttered a single improper word.

When the vizier returned, he found the royal ring and was troubled by dark suspicions, withdrawing from his wife.

The lady brought the matter before the king’s public tribunal in an allegorical suit: "O King! I had a fertile garden which I guarded with honor. A lion entered my garden and departed without trampling a single petal; yet my husband refuses to enter his orchard in fear of the lion’s paw!"

The king stood before the court and declared: "The lion entered your garden, O lady, and found it guarded by an angel of virtue; he departed with clean claws and bowed head. Let your husband return to his orchard with joyous pride!" The vizier understood, and their household flourished in restored honor.'
moral: Respect for the domestic sanctity of loyal servants is the hallmark of a noble monarch.

quiz.question: What is the central moral lesson taught in "The King and His Wazir's Wife"?
options: Presence of mind and quiet wisdom triumph over brute strength.

Believing rumors and flattery without proof
